tasks.short: Check the application for completeness, check measurable rules, review structural and fire safety design, decide on approval, and write the approval letter.

steps.what: Building inspector checks the application for missing documents
Building inspector checks heights, setbacks and areas against the zoning rules
Building inspector reviews structural and fire safety design
Building inspector decides to approve building plans that meet required specifications
Building inspector writes the approval letter

tasks.design: The permit portal ({GOV_PORTAL}) checks by rule that every required document and field is present before an application reaches the inspector. Measurable items (height, setbacks, built area) are checked by code against the zoning plan data and the dimensions the applicant declares, and the inspector sees only the failures. The approval letter is generated from the decision fields. Reviewing structural and fire safety design and deciding stay with the inspector; no software approves a plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completeness and measurable rules were checked by hand on every application.
tasks.enabler_now: Zoning plans are published as data; permit portals check required documents.
tasks.still_hard: Declared dimensions can be wrong; drawings still need reading.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a design meets the rules but will not work on this plot.
tasks.altitude: The inspector reviews failures and design instead of checking every rule.

evidence.claim: Zoning plans published as data allow code checks of height, setbacks and built area.
A decision made solely by automated processing needs a basis under GDPR article 22; here the inspector decides.

assumptions: Boundary: from the application to the approval letter; objections and appeals are outside.
Input contract: zoning data current; fallback is checking by hand.
The inspector decides on every plan.
Applicants enter dimensions in about the time they did on forms.
research_questions: Do code checks agree with the inspector's own checks?

incremental.description: Building inspector checks declared dimensions on the drawings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex plans; high: simple extensions and dormers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the relevant drawings, review and interpret plans for compliance, look up the applicable rules, record findings, and discuss issues with the architect.

steps.what: Building inspector finds the relevant drawings in the application
Building inspector reviews and interprets plans, blueprints and site layouts for compliance with safety regulations
Building inspector looks up the applicable legal requirements
Building inspector records findings in a checklist
Building inspector discusses issues with the architect

tasks.design: Applications arrive with a standard drawing index (site plan, floor plans, sections, structural calculations), so the inspector does not search the upload for each drawing. A digital checklist per building type links each item to the rule text, and findings are ticked with the rule reference and a note. Interpreting plans and discussing issues stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings were searched in loose uploads and rules looked up separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Permit portals can require a drawing index; checklists can link rule texts.
tasks.still_hard: Architects name drawings in their own way.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a section drawing and seeing the escape route does not work.

reach.learn: Whether questions back to them fall.

evidence.claim: Permit portals can require a drawing index; digital checklists can link items to rule texts.

assumptions: Boundary: from the application to issues discussed; the decision is outside.
Input contract: applicants upload by drawing type; fallback is searching uploads.
Interpreting plans stays with the inspector.
Architects upload by type in about the time they took before.
research_questions: Are findings referenced to rules more consistently?

incremental.description: Building inspector keeps checklists in step with rule changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual buildings; high: standard housing plans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check fees and conditions, decide to issue the permit, write the permit with conditions, check it, send it to the applicant, and publish the notice.

steps.what: Building inspector checks that fees are paid and conditions are met
Building inspector decides to issue permits for construction, relocation, demolition or occupancy
Building inspector writes the permit with its conditions
Building inspector checks the final permit
Building inspector sends the permit to the applicant
Building inspector publishes the permit notice

tasks.design: The permit system ({OTHER}) shows payment status and a checklist of preconditions per case, so the inspector does not look them up in finance and the file. The permit is generated from a template with a library of standard conditions chosen per case. Once the inspector has checked the permit, it goes to the applicant through the portal and the notice is published from the same record. Deciding to issue stays with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment and conditions were checked across systems and permits typed with copied conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Permit systems show payment status and generate permits from condition libraries.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a condition that protects neighbours without blocking the build.
tasks.altitude: The inspector chooses conditions instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Permit systems can show payment status and generate permits from a library of standard conditions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the approved plan to the notice published; objections are outside.
Input contract: payments linked to the case; fallback is checking finance.
The inspector decides and checks every permit.
research_questions: Do permits go out sooner after approval?

incremental.description: Building inspector keeps the condition library current.

approvals.approved_version: The permit as checked by the inspector in s4.
The permit as checked by the inspector in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: permits with many special conditions; high: standard permits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan site visits with contractors, monitor installation of plumbing, wiring and equipment on site, record findings, and order corrections.

steps.what: Building inspector plans site visits with contractors by phone
Building inspector monitors installation of plumbing, wiring, equipment or appliances on site
Building inspector records findings on paper and types the report
Building inspector orders corrections where installation does not comply with regulations

tasks.design: Contractors book inspection moments in the permit portal from the inspector's open slots, so visits are not planned by phone. Findings are recorded on a tablet checklist with photos at the site, and the report is generated from it. Inspecting installations and ordering corrections stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visits were planned by phone and findings typed up at the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Permit portals can offer booking; tablet checklists produce reports.
tasks.still_hard: Building sites run late and visits move.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a gas pipe run that the drawing does not show.

evidence.claim: Permit portals can offer booking of inspection moments; tablet checklists produce reports with photos.
GPS and time stamps in a crew app monitor attendance and performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the inspection due to corrections ordered; enforcement is outside.
Input contract: open slots kept by the inspector; fallback is phone.
Contractors book online in about the time a call took; a little contractor time is priced.
Inspecting on site does not change.
research_questions: Do reports go out on the day of the visit?

incremental.description: Building inspector keeps open inspection slots current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few visits; high: many short visits per day.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The building inspector keeps reviewing design, interpreting plans, deciding on permits and inspecting sites; completeness checks, rule look-ups, typed permits and phone planning shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An inspector with more time on site.
